These appeals coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER
By this common order, Miscellaneous Appeal No.1413/2016 filed by the insurance company shall be also decided.

2. Both the miscellaneous appeals under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act have been filed against the award dated 16.03.2016 passed by Member Second Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhatarpur in Claim Case No.88/2015 by which the claim petition has been allowed and an amount of Rs.2,57,000/- with 6% interest has been awarded.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal has been filed by the insurance company seeking exoneration on the ground that the accident took place on 07.04.2012 and the right hand of the appellant got amputated as it was stuck in the thresher.

2
4. It is submitted that thresher was not insured by the appellant.
However, it is fairly conceded that thresher was connected with the tractor which was insured by the appellant.

5. In the case of Kishore Vs. Shahid Shah decided on 09.08.2010 in M.A. No.1935/2005, this Court has held that if thresher is attached to a tractor, then the insurance company of the tractor can be held to be liable.

6. Accordingly, it is held that the Claims Tribunal did not commit any mistake by holding that the insurance company is jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation alongwith the respondent no.1.
Accordingly, the appeal filed by the insurance company is hereby dismissed.
This appeal has been filed by the claimant for enhancement of compensation amount.
8. It is submitted that undisputedly the right hand of the appellant has been amputated.

It is true that the appellant could not file any document in support of his treatment but looking to the injuries sustained by the appellant, an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards the treatment as well as the doctor fee is on a lower side and it should be enhanced.

It is further submitted that amount of Rs.10,000/-
awarded towards attendant, special diet etc. and an amount of Rs.10,000/- awarded towards mental pain and agony is also on a lower side.
9.
Per contra, the counsel for the respondent No.2/insurance company has supported the quantum of compensation awarded by the Claims tribunal.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
11.
Medical prescription, Exhibit P/5 has been filed according to which the appellant had suffered traumatic amputation of right proximal 1/3rd forearm.
The MLC which was prepared on the date of accident and was filed alongwith the criminal case is Exhibit P/4.
Thus, the amputation of right hand of the appellant from proximal 1/3rd forearm is not in dispute.
The appellant must have spent a considerable amount towards his treatment.
However, it is equally true that no document of treatment has been filed.
It is also possible that the appellant might have got himself treated in a Government Hospital.
12. Be that whatever it may be.
13. The amount of Rs.25,000/- which has been awarded towards doctor fee/treatment appears to be on a lower side.
14. Taking a sympathetic view, this Court is of the considered opinion that the appellant is entitled for Rs.45,000/- towards doctor fee and treatment.
Rs.10,000/- has been awarded towards attendant charges, special diet etc.
Since the appellant had suffered the amputation of right upper limb, therefore, he must have been prescribed special diet and somebody must have stayed in the hospital for attending the appellant.

Accordingly, the amount of Rs.10,0000/- awarded under the head of attendant, special diet etc. appears to be on a lower side and accordingly, Rs.30,000/- is Kamlesh Yadav vs Jayram Yadav on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69179669/
3 awarded under the said head.
Undisputedly, the appellant had suffered traumatic amputation of right proximal 1/3rd forearm.
Under these circumstances, this court is of the considered opinion that Rs.10,000/- awarded under mental pain and agony is on a lower side.
Accordingly, Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards mental pain and agony.

Thus, the appellant is entitled for the following compensation amount:
 S.No.
Head Amount  1. Permanent disability Rs.2,00,000/- as awarded by  the Claims Tribunal.

2. Doctor fee/treatment Rs.45,000/-
 3. Attendant, Special diet Rs.30,000/-
 etc.
 4.
Mental pain and agony Rs.50,000/-

5. Total Amount Rs.3,25,000/-
15.
Thus, the compensation of Rs.2,57,000/- awarded by the Claims tribunal is enhanced by a further amount of Rs.68,000/-.
The remaining conditions of the award shall remain the same.
16. With aforesaid modification, the award dated 16.03.2016 passed by Member Second Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chhatarpur in Claim Case No.88/2015 is hereby affirmed.
